title: First European trip with Ellington in 1933
summary: Europe with Duke in 1933 or 1934 was a thrill; they played only two shows at the London Palladium and ducked the crowds at the stage door.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When was the first time you went to Europe? It was with Duke, wasn't it?
Yeah, it was '33 or '34, something like that.
'33, I think, was the band's first trip to Europe. What was that like?
Oh, that's quite a thrill. We played that -- what's that theater over there? We only played two shows -- one show -- two shows, yeah, in England, in London.

Palladium, yeah. We played two shows there and that was it. And then you had to try to duck to get out the theater because everybody hangs around the stage door, so a lot of times I used to go through the front and go out

that way.
It's a thrill when you're young and you haven't had anything like that happen to you in life. But then after you have it a few times, you get tired of it.
